launcher: The launcher is now Orre Launcher, for Pokémon Colosseum and XD: its new name shows in the top bar, the window title and Discord. Your settings, games and saves stay where they were.

Pokédex: each Pokémon shows its whole evolution family, from its first stage to its last with every branch, and what each evolution needs: a level, a stone, a trade, friendship, or a move it must know. Where the game can't make an evolution, such as Feebas's by Beauty, it says so, and a Generation 4 evolution made a level says how Pokémon Platinum had it. Click a Pokémon in the family to open it.

Jukebox: a new tab plays the game's music from your disc. Pick a song and a small player appears along the bottom of every page, with previous, play and pause, stop, next, Loop and volume, so the music keeps playing while you build a team or change settings. A second tab plays the game's sound effects (menu, battle and, in Colosseum, movement sounds) from the disc too, in Colosseum and in XD. Both tabs have a search box, filters for tunes, battles and jingles or for each group of effects, a Sort menu (by name, type or length), and three views to pick from: a grid of square cards with each song's disc large at the top, a list with columns, or a compact list. Press the star beside any song, or in the player, to add it to your Favorites, and again to take it out. The Favorites tab plays them through in order or shuffled, with Loop starting again after the last; drag songs or use the arrows to reorder them. Each game keeps its own Favorites. Each song has a cover shaped like a GameCube disc, and the one in the player spins while the music plays (it stays still if you have reduced motion turned on). Each song shows how long it is, the short jingles are listed after the tunes, and the player is one thin row whose bar shows where you are in the song and can be dragged to skip around. Close the player with its X; starting the game stops the music. The music plays in the launcher, so the game doesn't need to be set up or running.

Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness: pick Colosseum or XD on the Play page, and the launcher sets up and plays that game from your own North American disc (GXXE01). Each game has its own setup folder, disc and memory card, and your Colosseum setup stays as it was. If you saved XD on Colosseum's memory card in an earlier Beta, that save moves to XD's own card by itself, after a backup. XD is early: its renderer, display, controller, frame rate, widescreen, HD text, fast-forward and Skip movies settings apply, and so does Later generations under Gameplay: its Gen 4 battle rules, Pokémon and moves come to XD from your Colosseum disc, each Gen 4 Pokémon looking and sounding like one of XD's own. Colosseum's other extras, such as HD trainer models and language packs, are hidden while XD is chosen.

The Play page shows both games, split by a diagonal line: the game you choose fills most of the window in full colour, and the other waits faded at the side. XD has its own painting, the wrecked S.S. Libra in the desert under the moon. Each side shows that game's title logo, read from your own disc (in HD when the HD textures have it), or its name until you've chosen its disc: large in the middle of the side you chose, above Play, and large in the middle of the other side's strip too; while you set a game up, its logo waits small at the top to leave room for the steps. Click the other side or its logo and the line sweeps across, the logos gliding and growing or shrinking into place with it; on a controller, press X (Square on PlayStation).
Choosing the other game's disc switches the Play page to that game, instead of turning the disc down.
Saves: Pokémon XD saves export to Dolphin as a .gci file and import from one, as Colosseum's do. Choose XD on the Play page, then use Import or Export on the Saves tab.

Discord: Pokémon XD shows on your Discord profile too, under XD's own name with its own picture of the place you're in, the trainer you're battling and your lead Pokémon, when Discord activity is on under Settings.

Pokémon XD: battle animation speed and Skip battle animations, Quick moves and quick status effects, shiny Shadow Pokémon and Choose starter now work in XD too, from the same settings under Gameplay. In XD a Shadow Pokémon can be shiny, which the original never allows, and a New Game asks whether to begin with Eevee.

Pokémon XD: Generation 4 Pokémon take their models and cries from your Battle Revolution disc in XD too, Yanma, Aipom and Piloswine can evolve as in Platinum, and Pokémon packs work in XD. All of it is made from your Colosseum disc, so set that up as well.

Online: Pokémon XD battles online too, with a party from the team builder, which reads its Pokémon from your Colosseum disc. Tick Colosseum and XD players can join when you create a room, and a player of either game can battle you. XD's online battles have Colosseum's turn and battle timers, the Pokémon selection screen with team preview, the trainers' screens before and after a battle, and the sleep and HP clauses. In a room for both games every Pokémon is one both games have the same: the 386 Pokémon of the third generation, no Shadow Pokémon or Shadow moves, and only held items both games have, so the battle goes the same on both screens. XD's rooms, and rooms for both games, can also play by Pokémon Platinum's battle rules, with a Generation 4 party's Pokémon, moves and held items. The launcher says what a party would have to change before you create or join one, and a Story party's other Pokémon stay home. Both players need the same version of the games.

Pokémon XD: the randomizer works in XD too, from the same settings under Gameplay. It can swap your Eevee, the Shadow Pokémon, trainers' Pokémon, and the Pokémon traded to you and Mt. Battle's Chikorita, Cyndaquil and Totodile; Lugia, the Shadow Togepi you're given, Poké Spots, Quick Battle and the battle CDs stay as they are. The launcher reads your XD save's seed, and Show spoilers works for an XD run.

Online: your Story party works in Pokémon XD too. Choose XD on the Play page, and the Online page offers the party from your XD save, each Pokémon with its moves, nature, IVs, EVs, held item and nickname; Shadow Pokémon stay home until they're purified.

Game Boy Advance: link your Ruby, Sapphire, Emerald, FireRed or LeafGreen save to Pokémon XD too, and trade at the Trade Center in a Pokémon Center's basement. Set it up under Settings → Game Boy Advance, on socket 2.

Pokémon XD: the Pokédex and the Jukebox work in XD too, read from your XD disc. The Pokédex shows XD's own models, sprites and cries, and says how XD gives each Pokémon: your Eevee, a trade or Mt. Battle reward, a Shadow Pokémon to snag, a Poké Spot, or an evolution. The Jukebox plays the songs of XD's own sound test, looping as the game does. Most of XD's songs now show their names (Gateon Port, Cipher Battle, Shadow Lugia Battle and so on) instead of the disc's file names.

Pokémon XD: HD textures work in XD too: every texture on XD's disc, upscaled 4× the way Colosseum's are, from Pokémon, trainers' faces and menus to every town. With HD textures on under Settings → Graphics, XD downloads them the next time you play it: about 3.8 GB, in two parts.
Online: Beta now builds Colosseum and Pokémon XD from the same newest game, so players of either game can join a room for both games.

Battle Revolution assets: the launcher checks the disc file you choose straight away. A file that isn't Pokémon Battle Revolution, such as your Colosseum disc, another Wii game or a ZIP, is turned down with the reason in a banner under Settings → Gameplay and in the Generation 4 prompt, instead of failing minutes into making the assets, and a copy that looks cut short gets a warning. A wrong disc chosen before shows a banner on the Play page too.

Pokémon XD: with HD textures on, the name screen's title bar is an even dark grey, as it is without the pack, instead of getting darker toward its right end. The launcher takes that one texture out of the installed pack, so nothing needs downloading again.

Add to Steam: Pokémon XD gets a Steam shortcut of its own, with its own name and artwork, that starts XD. Choose XD on the Play page and select its Add to Steam banner, which now sits on the chosen game's side. A Colosseum shortcut with Skip Launcher now always starts Colosseum, whichever game you chose last in the launcher.

Online: watch other players' battles. A battle under way on the room list has a Watch button, or type a room code and choose Watch. Your game plays the battle from its start, with the players' screens and battle camera but none of their menus, and fast-forwards to catch up if you come in late. You don't need a party to watch, the players see how many are watching, and Stop watching leaves.
TMs by move name: a new switch under Gameplay, on by default, for listing TMs by the moves they teach in the bag and shops. Turn it off to see TM24 and the rest again.

Choose your hero: a new switch under Gameplay, on by default, for the question a New Game asks about who you will play as. It's there for Colosseum and XD. Turn it off to start every New Game as the game's own hero (Wes, or Michael in XD); a save keeps the hero it was made with either way, unless you choose a hero for the story on the Customize page.

Customize: a new tab where you can try out colours for Wes, Brendan, May, Red and Leaf, and in Pokémon XD for Michael too, on their 3D models from your disc, with presets and a colour for each part of their outfit, saved as you go. Pick a motion to watch them move as they do in the game, legs bending and stepping (Idle, the Poké Ball and Snag Ball throws and more), pause and step through it, and tick Wes's moves to see a Game Boy Advance hero move exactly as Wes does. Online battles show you as your hero in your colours, in Colosseum and XD: press Battle online as on any hero to battle as them, or keep the hero your save plays as. Press Play the story as to play every save as that hero, even saves made before or as someone else, until you press Use each save's own hero. The story shows your heroes in their colours too, in the field, in battle and on the menus, with or without the HD textures.
The launcher opens the way you left it: full screen (F11) or maximized, instead of always in a window.

Fixed Steam's on-screen keyboard popping up on a Steam Deck when the game starts, and when the controller moved onto a text box in the launcher. A text box now waits until you press A on it before the keyboard opens.

Fixed the Settings page scrolling back to the top by itself while a GameCube controller adapter, such as Mayflash's, was plugged in. Controllers that are plugged in but not being used no longer move the page or the highlighted setting.

Randomizer: two new switches, both off to start with. No repeats keeps any evolution family from coming up twice among the Pokémon you start with and the Shadow Pokémon, and with Trainers' Pokémon on, from coming up twice in one trainer's team. First forms only makes your starters and the Shadow Pokémon Pokémon that don't evolve from another, so you can raise and evolve them. Find both under Randomizer in Settings; they apply from your next New Game.

Settings has a new Sound tab, with Master volume, Music and Sound effects sliders for the game. They are the same sliders as on the game's new Settings screen. Anything you change on that screen, sound or picture, is saved to the launcher's Settings straight away, while you play.
Fixed online rooms on Platinum's rules (Generation 4) starting their battles without Platinum's rules, moves and Pokémon.

Online replays: every online battle you play or watch is saved, and the Online page has a new Replays tab beside Rooms that lists them. Press Watch and the game plays the battle again from its start, with each player as the hero they battled as. A bar above the game marks every turn and where Pokémon fainted: click a turn to jump to it, step back or ahead a turn, pause, and pick a speed from 0.5x to 8x. The last 50 battles are kept, and starring one keeps it for good. To share a battle, send its file (Show folder finds it). Open replay, or dropping the file on the Online page, adds one someone sent you. A replay saved with another version of the game plays until that version's battle goes differently, then stops and says so.

Windows: when Windows can't start one of the build's programs (error 0xC0000142), the launcher builds again with fewer programs at once, and if that fails too it says what usually causes it: antivirus, overlays or screen recorders that load themselves into every program.

Windows: if the game folder has an accented letter in its path, such as the é in Pokémon Colosseum, and the game version being set up can't be built there, setup now stops at once and says to move it to a folder like C:\Games, instead of failing at the end of the build.

Pokémon XD: playing as Wes, Brendan, May, Red or Leaf, your hero throws Poké Balls with Michael's throw, so the ball leaves their hand and flies over their head, where it used to come out of their chest.
Pokémon XD: playing as Wes, Brendan, May, Red or Leaf, the Snag Ball now flashes into your hero's palm as it does in Michael's hand, where it used to sit inside their fist from the start.
Later generations: in Pokémon XD, Generation 4 and pack Pokémon icons in Pokémon Storage and the Purification Chamber are now as big as XD's own Pokémon beside them, instead of noticeably smaller.
Settings: the Performance overlay switch is now Controls overlay, as the overlay lists your controls.
game: Online: each player battles as their own hero in the colours they chose on the launcher's Customize page, in Colosseum and XD and in rooms for both games, and both players and anyone watching see them that way, even when both picked the same hero. Michael shows only in XD: in Colosseum a player who chose him appears as the game's usual trainer, and so does a player on an older launcher.
Frame rate: Pokémon XD's overworld and battles run at 60 fps too, where they used to stay at 30, at the original game's speed. Choose 30 or 60 fps under Frame rate in Settings.

Pokémon XD: press A to skip The Pokémon Company and Genius Sonority logos and the opening movie, as in Colosseum, and in widescreen the two logos fill the screen with their background colour instead of black bars.

Pokémon XD: HD text draws XD's text sharp from the Inter typeface, as it does Colosseum's, where it used to only smooth the original letters. It's on by default; choose Text under Gameplay to change it.
Pokémon XD: fixed your character stuttering while walking or running at 60 fps.
Online: in a room for both games, Colosseum makes every Pokémon by the same list of Pokémon, moves and held items as XD does, so both games battle with the same Pokémon.
Online battles now check the battle itself at every turn, so two games that drift apart end the battle instead of playing on with different HP.
Pokémon XD: fixed battles between two of the game's trainers never ending, such as ZOOK and ARDOS at Gateon Port, where neither ever chose a move.
Pokémon XD: fixed walls and furniture in the HQ lab popping in and the room looking squeezed at the 16:10 screen format.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game crashing as it started on some Linux PCs, with some graphics drivers and overlays.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game crashing in battle while it loaded a Pokémon or a move, such as when a Generation 4 Pokémon used Quick Attack.
Pokémon XD: fixed Pokémon and trainers disappearing in battles with Generation 4 Pokémon, leaving only a shadow or part of a trainer's hair.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game staying on a black screen as it started on Windows.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game freezing on a dimmed screen when you saved in some buildings, such as the house where you get an evolution stone and the diner in Gateon Port.

Pokémon XD: fixed the game crashing when you opened Pokémon Storage at a PC. Generation 4 Pokémon and Pokémon from packs show their own icons in the boxes, from your Battle Revolution disc or the pack's body sprite, where they used to show the Pokémon they stand in for.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game crashing after you had moved between rooms and areas about 64 times in one session, such as when leaving a house in Agate Village.
Pokémon XD: fixed the black band behind the name screen and the Continue screen stopping a few pixels short of the right edge.

Pokémon XD: fixed moves such as Sludge Bomb, Shadow Ball and Psychic playing with no effect, and Shadow Pokémon missing their purple aura when they're revealed in battle: the sludge, the ball, the burst on the target and the aura show again.

Pokémon XD: in widescreen, the Pokémon summary's panels no longer drop back to 4:3 for a moment as you turn its pages, and with the HD textures on, the grey band beside the Pokémon is one shade and the dark blocks in the bottom right corner are gone.
Pokémon XD: the randomizer's Pokémon packs option now works, so your packs' Pokémon can turn up in a randomized run.
Pokémon XD: the ending and the credits can be skipped with A or fast-forward, like the other movies.
Pokémon XD: fixed people's shadows in Realgam Tower being cut off in widescreen.
Pokémon XD: in four-trainer battles in widescreen, the second trainers' Poké Ball rows now sit at the screen edges under their panels.
Pokémon XD: fixed Pokémon and people shown in menus looking squeezed in widescreen, such as on the name screen, the Continue screen, the summary, the PC and the P★DA.
Pokémon XD: online battles can play by Pokémon Platinum's battle rules with a Generation 4 party, against another XD player or a Colosseum player in a room for both games.
Pokémon XD: while you wait online for a challenger, the game shows its menu backdrop and Waiting in room with your room code, instead of a black screen.
Pokémon XD: when the other player leaves an online battle while you choose, the battle ends and says so, instead of leaving your menu open.
Pokémon XD: on the online team-pick screen, the stick and the keyboard's arrow keys pick Pokémon, and the buttons shown match your controller or keyboard.
Pokémon XD: Quick moves work in VS MODE's Quick Battle: press Z, then A, B, X and Y pick moves.
Pokémon XD: under Platinum rules, a move's details in Quick Battle show whether it is PHYSICAL, SPECIAL or STATUS.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game crashing on Windows in battle when a Pokémon was sent out.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game crashing on an opposing trainer's turn in some double battles, when the trainer had a pair of moves it plays together, such as Sweet Scent and Blizzard.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game crashing at 60 fps as a battle with a Mt. Battle Area Leader, such as Vander, began.

Shader warm-up works now, in Colosseum and in XD: the game builds the effects it is known to use before it draws them, all of them in the background from the logos on with Metal and Vulkan, so new places and battles no longer stutter the first time you play on a computer.

Online: a spectator's game plays the battle as the players' games do, and while the players choose, its text box says Players are selecting moves... (or which player is choosing a Pokémon after a faint), in Colosseum and Pokémon XD.

The bag and shops list a TM by the move it teaches, such as THUNDERBOLT, instead of TM24, and while one is selected its number shows in a tab above the description box. This works in Colosseum and XD.

Cheats: press F9 while playing for a cheat menu, in Colosseum and XD. It has Infinite HP, One-Hit KO, Infinite PP, EXP and money multipliers, Always Snag, Snag Any Pokémon (snag a trainer's ordinary Pokémon too), Shiny Shadow Pokémon, Fast Purification, Heal Party and Walk Speed. Cheats start off each time you play, aren't saved, and are off in online battles.
Warp: press F8 while playing to pick any place in the game and go straight there, in Colosseum and XD. Save first, as warping ahead of the story can leave it stuck.

Choose your hero: a New Game now asks who you will play as before the name screen, Wes or a Game Boy Advance hero (Brendan, May, Red or Leaf), shown turning in 3D. Your hero walks the story, shows on the name screen and the Continue screen, and throws Poké Balls and Snag Balls in battle; the save remembers who you chose. The opening, the movies and the P★DA's trainer card still show Wes (online, you battle as the hero you choose on the Customize page), and the close-up of the Snag Machine before a snag shows only the wall behind your hero. In Pokémon XD the name screen asks first, Michael or Wes, Brendan, May, Red or Leaf, each shown on the screen's own model: your hero walks and runs the story with Michael's moves, battles, snags with Michael's own Snag Ball throw (holding the ball up to the camera as he does), and shows on the name and Continue screens, while the P★DA, the world map and the battle's opening faces still show Michael.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game crashing on Macs with Apple silicon as an opponent chose its moves in some double battles, such as at the second turn of the battle with Gorigan.

Generation 4 rules: fixed the game crashing or freezing when you tried to switch out a Pokémon held in by a foe's Shadow Tag, Arena Trap or Magnet Pull, such as a Wobbuffet's. The game now says the Pokémon can't switch out, in Colosseum and XD.

Fixed setting up the game on Windows stopping with "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'splitlines'" when a build tool printed letters Windows' code page couldn't read, such as an accented name in the folder path.
Fixed setting up the game on Windows stopping near the end with "Cannot find source file" and a CHANGES file, on PCs that have unix2dos installed with tools such as Git or MSYS2.
Randomizer: runs can have no repeated evolution families and first-form starters and Shadow Pokémon. With both off, a seed chooses the same Pokémon as before.

In Colosseum, Generation 4 Pokémon close their eyes when they fall asleep, open them when they wake and blink now and then while they wait, and their eyes and mouths change during moves, hits and fainting, as in Battle Revolution. Press Make assets when the launcher asks, to make their models again.

Under Pokémon Platinum's battle rules, a fainted Pokémon's replacement now comes out at the end of the turn, after the weather and the turn's other effects, as in Diamond, Pearl and Platinum, instead of straight away, and so does a trainer's next Pokémon after you snag one of theirs; a move whose target has fainted or been snagged by then turns to the other foe in a double battle, or says "But there was no target..." and still uses its PP. This is in Colosseum only for now: in Pokémon XD and in online rooms for both games, a replacement still comes out straight away.
Fixed U-turn saying an opponent's Pokémon went back to you: it now names the trainer the Pokémon went back to, in Colosseum and XD.

Later generations: fixed a Substitute looking like Turtwig, and Castform's rainy, sunny and snowy forms turning into Grotle, Torterra and Chimchar. In XD, Castform's forms and Shadow Lugia no longer turn into Turtwig, Grotle or Torterra.

Pokémon XD: fixed the game freezing on Windows as a TV's picture changed, such as when NETT hands the DATA ROM over during the raid at ONBS in Pyrite Town, and when you left the HQ lab by its door or elevator. If a frame ever fails to finish drawing, XD now skips it after a few seconds and plays on, instead of freezing.
On Linux, when the game can't open its window, the activity log and error box now give the real reason, such as a graphics driver that failed to load, instead of only "Invalid window".

Settings in the game: the field menu (START) has a new SETTINGS button above EXIT, in Colosseum and in XD. It opens a Settings screen over the game with three pages, Display, Graphics and Sound: fullscreen, aspect ratio, brightness, V-Sync, resolution, anti-aliasing, upscaling, HD textures and more change while you play, and Sound has separate Master volume, Music and Sound effects sliders. Use the D-pad or stick to pick and change a setting, L and R to turn the page, and B to go back to the menu. What you change there is kept for next time.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game crashing on Windows just after some battles start, such as the Rider Willie fight outside the Outskirt Stand.

Replays of online battles play in Colosseum and in XD, with a bar across the top of the game showing the turn and how far through the battle it is. In the game, Start pauses, left and right go back or ahead a turn, and up and down change the speed.

Fixed story cutscenes stopping for good at 60 fps with someone walking on the spot, such as Beluh at the top of the stairs in Agate Village when she goes for the Small Tablet, and Miror B. at the door in Realgam Tower after his battle. Holding fast-forward is no longer needed to get past them.

Fixed the game crashing when a trainer spotted you and walked over while Rui stood in the way, such as at the top of the Under's elevator in Pyrite Town, and when you sorted your PDA e-mail by sender or by subject. Pokémon XD had the same fault where someone steps aside to make way, and it's fixed there too.

Later generations: Generation 4 move descriptions no longer run out of their boxes. Each is broken into lines that fit, as the game's own descriptions are, on the summary's moves page, the screen for forgetting a move and, in XD, the Move Teacher's list.

Later generations: Cherrim changes into its Sunshine Form in strong sunlight and back to its Overcast Form when the sun ends, in Colosseum and in XD. Press Make assets when the launcher asks, to make its Sunshine Form's model.

Windows: the game now builds when its folder has an accented letter in its path, such as the é in Pokémon Colosseum. Before, the build stopped with "stdlib.h: No such file or directory" or, at its last step, "cannot find".
Windows: when Windows fails to start one of the build's programs (error 0xC0000142), the build tries it again, and says what happened if it keeps failing.

Pokémon XD: playing as Wes, Brendan, May, Red or Leaf, the close-ups when your Aura Reader spots a Shadow Pokémon and when you throw a Snag Ball now show your hero's face and hand, where they used to show their chest or shoulder, and your hero no longer stoops over in them.
Pokémon XD: fixed the Disc Case in Key Items not letting you move between your Battle CDs, and the game freezing after you closed it.
Online battles in Pokémon XD use the same battle menus as the story: choose with the cursor and A, with no more picking moves with the right stick to hide them from your opponent.

Online team preview has a cursor in Colosseum and XD: move it with the D-pad, stick or arrow keys, press A to pick the Pokémon under it, B to take back your last pick and R to see its summary, instead of a different button for each Pokémon.

Later generations: Lava Plume and Discharge hit every Pokémon around the user in a double battle, both foes and its partner, as in Pokémon Platinum, in Colosseum and in XD. Under Colosseum's own battle rules they used to hit only one foe.

Later generations: fixed Shedinja taking no recoil from Struggle under Platinum's battle rules, which could leave a battle with no way to end. Struggle's recoil now always takes at least 1 HP, as in Pokémon Platinum.

Pokémon XD: in widescreen, the new P★DA mail, Poké Snack and ready-to-purify notices and the Miror Radar's icon keep their shape at the left edge of the screen, as on a 4:3 screen, instead of drawing their bar stretched far across it.

Later generations: in Pokémon XD, Generation 4 and pack Pokémon faces are round like XD's own, so an ear or the corners no longer stick out of the round portrait frame, such as Luxio's in the battle panel.

Fixed the game refusing to save at every start ("The game data can't be saved", or in XD "The POKéMON XD save file is corrupted") when the save file had been left empty, which could happen when the system went down soon after starting a new game. The empty file is moved aside and kept, so you can start a new save, and the game now writes each save in full before it replaces the old one, in Colosseum and in XD.
Pokémon XD: fixed the game crashing on Windows as soon as you picked an item to sell at a shop, such as at the Outskirt Stand or in Agate Village.

Fixed walking through walls with fast-forward on, such as coming out a level or two up beside the Pokémon Center in Agate Village, and in Pokémon XD out of the HQ lab beside the elevator or through a closed door. Fast-forward now plays more of the game's own steps instead of longer ones, so on a slower computer it may run a little slower than the speed you picked.

Fixed fast-forward and a faster Battle animation speed holding a battle up while each move's sound and each Pokémon's cry finished playing at normal speed. The battle now moves on as soon as the sped-up animation is over, and the sound still plays to its end, in Colosseum and in XD.

Pokémon XD: with Skip movies on, a new game goes straight past the opening scene of Shadow Lugia lifting the S.S. Libra and on to the battle simulation in the lab, as it does once the scene ends. Turn it on under Gameplay.

Pokémon XD: with the HD texture pack, the sea in the opening scene no longer looks like rough rock, and the helicopters' searchlights keep their soft glow. The game's own textures are used for these, as on the console.

Colosseum's Battle Mode in widescreen: the Pokémon selection screen and the VS screen before it fill the whole window instead of a 4:3 picture with black bars, their backdrop carried out to the sides at its own shape, and the title bars along the top of Battle Mode's menus, such as Battle Now, reach both edges.

The overlay the backtick key (`) opens is now a button guide, in Colosseum and XD: it lists your own keyboard keys and controller buttons for each GameCube button, the stick, the C-Stick, the D-pad, half tilt, fast-forward and the Game Boy Advance, including any you changed under Controls, with the frame rate below. It no longer lists mouse controls, Esc or F7, which did nothing in this game, and nothing in it is named after Super Mario Sunshine any more.
Pokémon XD: fixed the lightning on top of Kaminko's house stretching across the yard and following you to the door. It stays between the poles on his roof again.
Pokémon XD: the controller now rumbles wherever the game rumbles on a GameCube, such as when you use a scent on a Shadow Pokémon or turn on Rumble Feature in Options. Before, XD never rumbled.

launcher: Later generations: play by Pokémon Platinum's battle rules and add the 107 Generation 4 Pokémon. Turn each on under Settings → Gameplay.
Battle Revolution assets: Generation 4 Pokémon take their looks and cries from your own Battle Revolution disc. Without it, a Colosseum Pokémon stands in for each.
Team builder: give each Pokémon its own moves, held item, ability, nature, EVs and IVs. Bring teams in or out as Pokémon Showdown text. Open it with New party or Edit on the Online tab.
Online formats: Orre Colosseum, Hoenn Stadium and Gen 3 OU rooms, with their clauses and bans. Casual stays as it was, Customise changes any rule, and a room can be a best of 3 or 5.
Online timers: a room can have a turn timer and a battle timer, set when you create it.
Legal Pokémon: format rooms check each Pokémon's moves, held item, EVs and IVs, and say what's wrong. A host can turn the check off under Customise.

Generation 4 online: any room can play by Platinum's rules, and a Generation 4 party battles there with that generation's Pokémon, moves and held items. Choose the rules when you create a room, and Generation 4 at the top of the team builder.
Online battles: both players need this version of the launcher.
Pokémon packs: add Pokémon of your own making, with their own stats, moves, model, sprites and cry. Open the packs folder from the Pokédex, then pick one as a starter or let the randomizer choose it.
Pokédex: models look as they do in the game and blink, every Pokémon has a Shiny look, and Cry plays its cry. It also shows what a Pokémon evolves from.
Randomizer: a run can include Generation 4 Pokémon and the Pokémon of your packs. Tick Gen 4 and Pokémon packs under Randomizer.
Language: play in French, German, Spanish or Italian, or with a fan translation. Choose it under Settings → Gameplay.

Game Boy Advance: link a Generation 3 save to trade Pokémon, register a team and spend Poké Coupons. It works with Ruby, Sapphire, Emerald, FireRed and LeafGreen saves, chosen under Settings → Game Boy Advance, with no GBA BIOS or Game Pak.
Fast-forward: one press of L + R can keep it on, and it runs from 2× to 8×. Set both under Settings → Gameplay.

HD textures: an updated pack keeps the grain of ground and walls and the soft edges of move effects. It also fixes black lines in floors and dark edges on some textures. About 1.9 GB, it downloads the next time you play with HD textures on.
Windows: the game's program has its own icon. The launcher also says before building when the Setup files folder's path has an &, which the build can't use.
When the game stops itself after an error, the launcher says why.
Fixed the game drawing with OpenGL instead of Vulkan on a Steam Deck and other Linux PCs with a newer Mesa.

changes: Generation 4 battle rules: battles play as in Pokémon Platinum, with moves physical or special by themselves, its damage, abilities, held items such as Life Orb and Choice Scarf, and Generation 4's moves. The move list shows whether a move is physical, special or status.

Generation 4 Pokémon: the game's own Pokémon learn moves and evolve as in Platinum, so Yanma, Aipom and Piloswine can become Yanmega, Ambipom and Mamoswine. The Move Deleter at Mt. Battle can also make a Pokémon remember a level-up move.
Choose starters: a New Game asks whether to begin with Espeon and Umbreon. Say No to pick any two Pokémon. Turn the question off under Gameplay in the launcher.
Quick moves: press Z (R1 or RB) in battle to open your moves, then A, B, X or Y to use one. Buttons show as your controller or keyboard has them. It's on to start with; turn it off under Gameplay.
Quick status effects: a status condition or stat change shows where the move hit, without its own camera shot. It's on to start with; turn it off under Gameplay.
The PC has 10 boxes instead of 3, room for 300 Pokémon. Backups keep them all, and a save exported for Dolphin takes boxes 1 to 3.
Shiny Pokémon: a Shadow Pokémon that will be shiny once snagged looks shiny in battle, and Espeon and Umbreon can be shiny from a New Game. Both have switches under Gameplay.
Online battles: Battle Mode's screens surround a battle. Both trainers show before it, you pick your Pokémon on the game's own selection screen when the room has team preview, and the results follow.
Online rules: battles can be doubles and play by Battle Mode's clauses. They now have critical hits and Soul Dew's boost, as the original game's link battles do.
Randomizer: a Shadow Pokémon or trainer's Pokémon that held the item for its type now holds the one for its new type.
Fixed a number showing instead of the move's name when a Pokémon forgets a move in battle.
Fixed the gold labels on the save and Continue screens showing red.
Fixed the sandstorm, strong sunlight, the PDA and the name screen not filling widescreen.
Fixed a stretched box around Sweet Scent's and Confusion's ripple in widescreen.
Fixed the PDA's Snag List showing the original game's Shadow Pokémon in a randomized run.
Fixed the arrow keys and WASD picking nothing on the Pokémon selection screen before a battle.
Fixed PlayStation controllers stopping in the game on Windows a few seconds after it started.
Fixed the game crashing on Mac when a Pokémon's Wish came true.
Fixed a dull echo trailing behind move sounds such as Sing and Attract.
Fixed the game crashing at start-up without a reason when it couldn't read its disc file. It now says what's wrong.
Fixed setup failing with Xcode 26 or pandoc installed, or when Vulkan's downloads fail.

launcher: Online battles: open a room or join one on the new Online tab and battle another player, at level 50 or 100 with 3 or 6 Pokémon each. Build named parties of six from your Pokédex, and your game waits in the stadium until someone joins. The room list updates by itself, and Refresh checks right away.

Story party: battle online with the Pokémon you travel with. The Online tab shows the party in your save, set apart at the top, and brings each one along with its moves, nature, stats, ability, held item and nickname, at the room's level. A party of 3 to 5 can take rooms of 3 each, and Shadow Pokémon stay home until they're purified.
The top bar shows how many players are online. It comes from an anonymous check-in you can turn off under Settings → Launcher.

Show on Discord: while you play, your Discord profile shows where you are in Orre with a picture of the place, who you're battling and your lead Pokémon, and online battles show your opponent. The Discord app needs to be open. Turn it off under Settings → Launcher.

Pokédex: browse all 386 Pokémon from your own disc, turn their 3D models around, play their motions and see their shiny looks. It also shows how you can get each one, and locks those the game keeps out of reach. Find it in the new Pokédex tab.

Randomizer: start a New Game with different starters, Shadow Pokémon, trainers' Pokémon and gifts, chosen by a seed you can share. Limit it to the generations you like, keep Pokémon about as strong as those they replace, or leave legendaries out. Your save keeps its seed, so fights stay the same when you try again. Find it under Gameplay.
Export a save: carry on in Dolphin with a .gci file of your game. Find it in the Saves tab.
Battle animations: a speed slider from 1× to 5× in steps of 0.1, with 1.5× as the new default, and a Skip battle animations switch that greys it out. Find them under Gameplay.

Macs with Apple Silicon: the game now builds as a native program and draws with Metal, so it runs faster and Rosetta is no longer needed. Metal is the new default renderer on these Macs; Vulkan and OpenGL are still under Graphics. Intel Macs stay on Vulkan.
Fixed the portable launcher on Windows never finding the game's crash reports, so Settings → Launcher can now copy them for a bug report.
Fixed game updates started from Steam filling the activity log with Steam overlay errors, which could also hide why a build failed.
Fixed a crash report on Linux and the Steam Deck when you closed the game with Stop in Steam.

changes: Online battles: two players' games play one battle, with both choosing their moves at the same time, from the launcher's Online tab. A Story party's Pokémon keep their moves, nature, stats, ability, held item, nickname and Poké Ball, at the battle's level.
Save anywhere: the menu you open with Start has a new SAVE option above EXIT. It saves where you stand, and Continue puts you back on that spot.
Randomizer: a new save can be a randomized run, and the save keeps its seed.
Rui and most trainers now have their detailed models in the field too, with sharper faces and real fingers.
Battle animations can run at any speed from 1× to 5× in steps of 0.1.
Macs with Apple Silicon: the game runs natively, and the wipe into a trainer battle plays in full instead of going black.
The game tells the launcher where you are, who you're battling and your lead Pokémon, for Show on Discord.
When Vulkan can't start on Linux, the game now tries the desktop's other window system before falling back to OpenGL, and the message says why Vulkan couldn't start.
In widescreen, the menu you open with Start now sits at the right edge of the screen, as it does in 4:3.
Fixed Pokémon getting a different nature and gender than a GameCube would give them at the same moment, which also threw off the random rolls after it, such as trainers' teams and damage.
Fixed the game not opening its window on Linux with newer graphics drivers, and that error calling the game Super Mario Sunshine.
Fixed people and objects disappearing near the sides of the screen in widescreen.
Fixed the arrow for picking a target sitting away from the status panels in widescreen.
Fixed the stripes of Yes/No boxes stopping short, and the Poké Ball in a text box's corner drawing outside the box, in widescreen.
Fixed Pokémon blinking twice as often at 60 fps, which also used up the game's random numbers faster than on a GameCube.

launcher: HD models: Wes uses his detailed model in the field. Turn it off under Graphics.
The game now builds from the port's own copy of the decompilation.

changes: Wes now has his detailed battle model while walking around, with a sharper face and real fingers.
Fixed the Pokémon faces missing from the Battle Now team screen.
Fixed opposing trainers misjudging a side's conditions and level-based moves.
Fixed the second trainer on a side being mistaken for the first.
Fixed Pokémon faces staying in memory after being replaced.
Fixed the Pokédex seen and caught flags on Linux and macOS.
Fixed Poké Ball catch rates on Linux and macOS.
Fixed the blue background on the main menus and save screen stopping short of the sides in widescreen.
Fixed the PC menus leaving black bars at the sides in widescreen.
Fixed the game crashing when entering a new area after playing for a long time.
Fixed Rui getting stuck walking on the spot when you first enter the mayor's house in Phenac City, and people stalling the same way in other cutscenes.

launcher: Battle animations: moves, send-outs and HP bars play at 2× speed by default. Change to normal speed or 4×, or skip them, under Gameplay.
Add to Steam: play from your Steam library, Big Picture or Game Mode, with artwork. Find it on the main screen, on Windows and Linux.
Skip Launcher: Steam can start the game straight away, and --play does the same from any shortcut.
Graphics presets: Low, Medium, High, Ultra and Steam Deck set the picture all at once. Find them under Graphics.
Crash reports: copy the newest report for a bug report, under Launcher. They stay on your computer.

changes: Fixed a box appearing around the white ring in some battle moves. Their ripple effect now works too.
Fixed your partner walking behind you facing the wrong way on Linux and macOS.
Fixed battle timers always showing 0 on Linux and macOS.
Fixed the title menu's selection jumping to the next option instead of sliding on Linux and macOS.
Fixed reflective effects not showing on Linux and macOS, along with the title options' animation and the stick in the P★DA.
Fixed items and Poké Balls saying they were meaningless to use in battle, and the bag jumping to another pocket afterwards.
Fixed shop messages showing the wrong price and item, like nearly 2 billion for one Super Potion. Sales always paid the right amount.
Fixed the game crashing when you pressed Down in the P★DA's Strategy Memo list.
Installing and updating the game downloads less: it no longer fetches two extra repositories to build.
Battle animations can run at 2× or 4× speed or be skipped, with menus at normal speed and text up long enough to read.
Building the game is faster: its code now compiles once instead of twice, on Windows too.
Setting up the game is quicker: the fixes its code needs now come ready-made instead of being worked out on your computer.
Game updates that change only part of the build now reuse more of what was already compiled.
The first game build after this update takes longer, as it starts over with what it keeps between builds.
Fixed new builds on Linux and macOS leaving out small corrections to battle and menu code that only a rebuild picked up.
Fixed the battle move menu showing the first move's PP and type whichever move you highlighted.
The logo movies at startup now fill a widescreen display with their background colour instead of black bars.

launcher: Fixed Windows builds with your own MSYS2, set with the COLO_MSYS2_ROOT environment variable, looking for the game's compiler in a folder that MSYS2 doesn't have.
Fixed a game download stopping at Prepare port source when a newer game commit is chosen under Settings, Manage game, Game source.
Windows builds now use a compiler that also runs on Windows 7, which the previous one could not.
The first game build on Windows after this update takes longer, as it starts over with the new compiler.

changes: Fixed builds reporting success when the game's compiler couldn't run: they now stop and say why.
Fixed a rare build that left out part of the battle menus' code.
Fixed Battle Now's party check overwriting nearby memory, which stopped the game on Arch Linux.
Fixed the game failing as it started when built on Arch Linux and other systems not based on Debian.
Fixed the game not fully unloading map code it had finished with.

launcher: New launcher background: a painted copper engine out in the desert.
Game updates and rebuilds are much faster: the launcher keeps what it compiled and reuses it. Free up space under Settings, Manage game clears it.
Import a Dolphin save: drop your North American .gci save on the Saves tab, or the folder it is in, and carry on from there. Your current saves are backed up first.
Join our Discord server: the Discord button at the top of the launcher opens the invite in your browser.

changes: The first build of the game is faster too.
Fixed the game stopping on macOS when you arrive in Phenac City with HD textures at the highest resolution.

launcher: First release: set up and play the Pokémon Colosseum PC port from your own North American disc on Windows, macOS and Linux.
Three-step setup downloads everything it needs and builds the game on your computer. The disc image never leaves it.
HD textures: all 7,498 of the game's textures upscaled 4×, on by default. Turn them off under Settings, Graphics.
Settings for the screen format, frame rate, picture sharpness, controls, rumble and GameCube controller adapters.
Your saves are backed up before and after you play. Restore one from the Saves tab.

changes: Native PC port with movies, music and sound, HD text, widescreen, 60 fps and Vulkan or OpenGL rendering.
